US Federal Reserve lowers interest rates for third time this year

Published 2026-10-07 18:40 UTC

The US Federal Reserve has cut interest rates for the third time this year, lowering its benchmark rate by a quarter of a percentage point to a range of 3.25% to 3.5% amid growing concern about the health of the American jobs market.

The Fed's statement said downside risks to employment had risen, while inflation remained somewhat elevated. Two members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented, preferring to keep rates on hold.

Speaking in Washington, the Fed chair, Jerome Powell, said policymakers would watch incoming data closely before deciding on a further cut in December. Wall Street rallied after the decision and the dollar weakened against the pound and the euro.
